content:
maria: Quick question — ACME wants a guaranteed 120k tok/s contract in us-west. Do we have a standard translation from tok/s commit -> reserved GPU count? Need numbers for legal and sales by EOD.
aj: Short answer: yes, but depends on model family and p95 sustained numbers. For a conservative p95 profile we use 'sustained p95 tok/s per A100-equivalent' and then add headroom for autoscaling/queueing. :memo: 
sre-june: For recent rock models we've been using ~6k tok/s p95 per A100-eq as a conservative baseline (with our batching/KV caching). That includes a small margin for sequence length variance.
kevin: here's a quick calc I used last week — paste into convo: 
```
Assumptions:
- Target commit: 120,000 tok/s
- p95 sustained per GPU (A100-eq): 6,000 tok/s
- Operational headroom factor: 0.85 (reserve 15% for scheduling/spike safety)
Reserved GPUs = ceil(120000 / (6000 * 0.85)) = ceil(120000 / 5100) = 24 GPUs
Optional burst pool: recommend 20% extra for short spikes => +5 GPUs (or enable burst to shared capacity)
```
maria: Solid — can we justify 6k number to sales? Any recent telemetry? :eyes: 
aj: Yes — we pulled p95 telemetry from the prod model telemetry stream for the last 30 days. For redwood-40b-ish workloads with avg seq len ~60 we see 5.5–6.5k at p95 depending on batching settings. document link: https://internal.metrics/redwood/p95-throughput (internal)
sre-june: Two caveats: 1) region constraints — us-west has fewer spare A100-equivalents next quarter, so a 24-GPU reserved footprint might require capacity prebooking. 2) if customer uses higher seq lengths or many concurrent small chats, effective per-GPU throughput drops — we should size from the customer's 95th token-length percentile.
kevin: For billing/legal we also recommend offering a commit band: base reserved (24 GPUs) + burst credit pool (10–20% of base) billed on usage above base at a reduced overage rate. Simpler than trying to size for absolute peak.
maria: billing question — last invoice for ACME seemed off; they were charged higher than expected for reserved + overage. billing-bot, can you pull the breakdown for invoice #7782?
billing-bot: Invoice 7782: base reserved usage matched 24 GPUs for 28 days. Overage triggered on 5 days due to a spike; overage tokens = 14M; rate applied = committed-overage-tier-1. Full CSV posted to S3: s3://billing-exports/7782-breakdown.csv
maria: Thanks. Two action items: 1) ops to confirm 6k p95 baseline from the telemetry slice for ACME's model/profile (sre-june + aj). 2) finance to review invoice 7782 overage calc and propose contract language for burst credits (kevin + billing).
sre-june: I'll post the telemetry slice by lunchtime and include seq-length distribution and p50/p95/p99. If seq p95 > 120 we'll note that sizing needs bump.
aj: Also flagging network egress constraints — if ACME wants multi-region failover we need cross-region bandwidth and additional reserved capacity in fallback region. That could add ~10% to reserved count.
kevin: For the sales quote I'll prepare two SKUs: "Committed 24 GPUs (p95)" and "Burst credit 5 GPUs / 20%" with overage pricing and a 30-day review window.
maria: Perfect. If nobody objects I'll send this to sales/legal after we get the telemetry CSV. :thumbsup: 
ops-bot: Note added to ticket INFRA-3419: "ACME commit sizing proposal — waiting on telemetry and invoice validation"
kevin: One more thought — if customer is ok with a shorter commit (90-day) we can run a smaller commit + monitoring and renegotiate at renewal to avoid long prebooking in tight regions.
maria: Agreed. Closing loop after telemetry. Thanks all.
